To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
arsenic at its drinking water guideline value is genotoxic in the erythrocellular lineage of fish.
the arsenic exposure at its guideline value in drinking water is genotoxic in fishes.
the exposure of fishes to the arsenic content of its guideline value in drinking water, as estimated to pose minimum cancer risk to human, exhibited marked genotoxcicity in fishes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genotoxicity of arsenic in fishes, which may be used to assess the genoecotoxicity of arsenical compounds in aquatic ecosystems.
the genotoxic potential assessment of arsenic at various exposure levels including its guideline value for the first time in aquatic animals.
the genotoxic potential assessment of arsenic at the guideline exposure in aquatic animals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
arsenic at its maximum contaminant limit for drinking water is not a safe chemical for aquatic environment.
arsenic at its exposure level of 10  μg L−1 is genotoxic in fish.
the guideline value of arsenic in drinking water, which is considered as safe, is genotoxic to fishes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the guideline standard for arsenic in drinking water may not be safe and the piscine micronuleus assay could be an effective biomarker to monitor arsenic contamination in water.
the guideline value of 10 µg L−1 for arsenic in drinking water may be revised in view of the present results.
arsenic, at its guideline exposure level, is genotoxic to fishes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
arsenic in drinking water is a potent genotoxic carcinogen that may pose a significant health risk to the human population.
arsenic at its maximum contaminant level in drinking water is genotoxic to aquatic animals, and therefore the guideline standard for drinking water should be reconsidered.
the guideline value of arsenic (10 μg/L) in drinking water is not safe and may pose serious genotoxic hazard to humans.
